newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish zloty gains, eyes reaching parity level.
newsitem.headline: Polish zloty gains, eyes reaching parity level.

text.p: The zloty firmed more than half a percentage point against the basket in early Monday trade after official interest rates were increased and dealers said the Polish currency may have some more near-term gains in store.
They said the zloty, spurred by speculative buying after interest rates rose by two and 2.5 points to 27 and 24.5 percent as of Monday, may be headed toward the parity level.

"The market is nervous after the rate rise but zloty buying continues and I wouldn't be surprised it the local unit firmed to the zero (from) parity level," said Jaroslaw Dryjski, foreign exchange dealer at Bank Slaski SA.
At 0750 GMT the zloyty was at -0.23/-0.29 percent from the parity rate, against -0.70/-0.93 percent at opening and last week's close around -0.87 percent.
It was at 3.4560/00 to the dollar against opening's 3.4700/800 and at 1.8555/85 to the mark versus 1.8570/00.

Dealers said however, that the zloty's rise may not be sustained over a longer period of time as the county's external deficit continues to mount and foreign investors were wary of buyign Polish bills before parliamentary polls on September 21.
Some said that the zloty's range for the next several days should be between parity and minus one percent.
One-day deposit rates continued to hover just below the 25-percent level in early Monday trading as the money market had already largely discounted the rate rise, dealers said.
"Players are still testing the market for longer-term depo rates...but one-day money has found a comfort zone around 25 percent," said Malgorzata Sikora, dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.

At 0810 GMT overnight rates were at 24.70/24.90 percent and tomorrow/next were at 24.80/24.95 percent against opening's 24.20/24.55 percent and 24.80/24.90 percent. One-month depos were quoted at 24.60/25.60 percent.
